claim_traces.claim_text: "Arctic sea ice has declined significantly since satellite records began in 1979."
reasoning_steps: Scientific data and observational records from organizations such as NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) confirm that Arctic sea ice extent and volume have experienced a significant, downward long-term trend since continuous satellite monitoring began in 1979

Across the satellite era, sea ice extent (particularly the September minimum) has declined at an approximate rate of 10 to 13 percent per decade, representing a loss of roughly 40 percent of late-summer ice cover.
